simple.meaning: אֳנִי (ʼŏnîy) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a ship or (collectively) a fleet.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 9:26. The surrounding context includes kingship, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֳנִי (H590) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֳנִי (ʼŏnîy) / H590 is traced through 1 Kings 9:26, 1 Kings 9:27, 1 Kings 10:11, 1 Kings 10:22 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H590. oni אֳנִי noun masculine 1Kin 10:11 & feminine 10:22 collective Ships, fleet — absolute 1Kin 9:26 +; construct 10:11 +; — of Solomon 9:26-27 , called ׳א תַרְשִׁישׁ (i.e. large, sea-going vessels, such as sail to Tarshish) 10:22 (twice in verse); ׳א חִירָם 10:11 , 22 ; propelled by oars שַֿׁיִט׳א Isa 33:21 .
definitions.rootNote: probably from 579 (in the sense of conveyance );

occurrences.englishText: King Solomon made a fleet of ships in Ezion Geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
Hiram sent in the fleet his servants, sailors who had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.

The fleet of Hiram that brought gold from Ophir, also brought in from Ophir great quantities of almug trees* possibly an Indian sandalwood, with nice grain and a pleasant scent, and good for woodworking and precious stones.
For the king had a fleet of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet. Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish came, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
